classification.difficultyReason: Identify the highest reported pH as the least acidic reference, invert the logarithmic model for each sample and express the comparisons as concentration ratios relative to that reference.

content.prompt: Research the pH values of some acidic substances used in everyday life. Rank them from least acidic to most acidic, and use the least acidic one as your reference. Using $\mathrm{pH}=\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{1}{C}\right)$, where $C$ is the hydronium ion concentration in $\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$, write beside each substance how many times as high its concentration is as that of the reference.

answer.short:
Answers vary. If the reported pH values are milk 6, orange juice 3 and vinegar 2.5, that is the order from least to most acidic. Relative to milk, the concentration factors are $1$, $1000$ and $10^{7/2}$, respectively.

Raise 10 to the difference between the reference pH and the sample pH.
answer.worked:
Use the reported pH values to rank the samples from highest pH to lowest pH. The highest-pH sample is the reference. The model gives $C=10^{-\mathrm{pH}}$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{C_{\text{sample}}}{C_{\text{ref}}}&=\frac{10^{-\mathrm{pH}_{\text{sample}}}}{10^{-\mathrm{pH}_{\text{ref}}}}\\\frac{C_{\text{sample}}}{C_{\text{ref}}}&=10^{\mathrm{pH}_{\text{ref}}-\mathrm{pH}_{\text{sample}}}\end{align*}$$

For illustration, suppose the reported pH values are 6 for milk, 3 for orange juice and 2.5 for vinegar. Milk is the reference. In order from least to most acidic, the concentration factors are milk $10^{6-6}=1$, orange juice $10^{6-3}=1000$ and vinegar $10^{6-2.5}=10^{7/2}$.
